- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.25) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% per day of bearish sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights early sentiment; weight recent 7-day sentiment more heavily than 18-day average.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.25–0.67) and price is trending sideways, model tends to overpredict volatility; smooth forecast curve with 3-day moving average.
